events.subtitle: Beethoven: Complete Violin Sonatas — three-night Carnegie Hall cycle

venue.name: Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage at Carnegie Hall

priority_review.rationale: The scarcity is the specific Carnegie Hall cycle, not classical-star fame by itself. Carnegie Hall is pairing Maxim Vengerov and Martha Argerich for all 10 Beethoven violin sonatas across three consecutive nights as part of Vengerov's Perspectives series, while Argerich returns to Carnegie Hall for the first time in a decade. That combination of complete-cycle scale, two living masters and a long-delayed Carnegie return makes A+ feel too casual for the likely regret if missed. The duo has performed the cycle in Hamburg and is scheduled to present it in Paris, and New York offers three nights, so S rather than S+ is the appropriate scarcity tier.

events.category: Living masters / Complete chamber cycle / Beethoven
events.factual_description: Carnegie Hall's 2026-27 season presents Maxim Vengerov and Martha Argerich on April 23, 24 and 25, 2027 in Stern Auditorium / Perelman Stage for Beethoven's complete sonatas for violin and piano. The three-concert cycle is part of Vengerov's artist-led Carnegie Hall Perspectives series. Carnegie Hall's official season announcement identifies these as Argerich's first performances at the Hall in 10 years. The same Vengerov-Argerich Beethoven cycle was performed across five evenings at the Martha Argerich Festival in Hamburg in June 2026, confirming that the complete-cycle collaboration is an active artistic project rather than an inferred one-off concept.

enrichment.note: Carnegie Hall's exact April 23 event page and official season announcement verify the three-night April 23-25 cycle, venue, complete Beethoven-sonata concept, Vengerov Perspectives context and Argerich's first Carnegie performances in 10 years. Current authoritative listings indicate 8:00 PM on April 23-24 and 7:00 PM on April 25, but the automation could not reliably resolve all three Carnegie event pages without redirect errors, so the canonical candidate leaves showtimes empty rather than promoting secondary timing into a factual field. en.why_it_matters: The event is the cycle, not a star recital with familiar repertoire. Beethoven's ten violin sonatas trace an enormous change in what violin and piano can demand from one another, and Vengerov and Argerich are taking that whole arc across three consecutive Carnegie nights. Argerich's first return to the Hall in a decade adds real historical weight, but the stronger musical reason is the sustained duo conversation: three evenings in which two highly individual players have to keep renegotiating balance, attack, freedom and structure across an entire body of work rather than one showcase sonata.
en.trip_verdict: Protect at least one night if a New York trip is remotely feasible, and consider the full three-night cycle if Beethoven chamber music is a central listening thread. The commitment is larger than a normal regional concert, but the complete-cycle format and Argerich's long Carnegie absence make it a legitimate anchor for a dedicated New York weekend rather than something to squeeze around another plan.

es.why_it_matters: El acontecimiento es el ciclo completo, no un recital de estrellas con repertorio conocido. Las diez sonatas para violín de Beethoven recorren un cambio enorme en lo que violín y piano se exigen mutuamente, y Vengerov y Argerich van a atravesar todo ese arco durante tres noches consecutivas en Carnegie Hall. El regreso de Argerich después de una década le añade peso histórico, pero la razón musical más fuerte es la conversación sostenida del dúo: tres noches obligados a renegociar balance, ataque, libertad y estructura a lo largo de un cuerpo completo de obra, no sólo en una sonata de exhibición.
es.trip_verdict: Protegería por lo menos una noche si un viaje a Nueva York es razonablemente posible, y consideraría el ciclo completo si la música de cámara de Beethoven está en el centro del hilo de escucha. El compromiso es mayor que para un concierto regional normal, pero el formato integral y la larga ausencia de Argerich en Carnegie hacen que pueda anclar un fin de semana dedicado en Nueva York, no simplemente acomodarse alrededor de otro plan.
